A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SP4D work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The appendices match after accounting for the checklist inserted in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation comparisons, ablations, and user studies in Tables 1–2, plus 3D segmentation and rigging results in Appendix C, Tables 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including all four tables and the appendix user studies.

M1.justification: The dual-branch architecture, BiDiFuse, spatial color encoding, contrastive loss, segmentation post-processing, and 2D-to-kinematic-mesh procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training and evaluation coverage: ObjaverseDy, KinematicParts20K, DAVIS examples, and generated objects, with the same segmentation, rigging, and animation tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: SAM2, SAM2*, and DeepViT in Table 1; SAM2 and DeepViT in Table 2; Segment Any Mesh and SAMPart3D in Table 3; Magic Articulate and UniRig in Table 4.

E3.justification: Training budgets, rendering settings, evaluation metrics, Hungarian matching, and testing procedures are unchanged. Appendix D.2 retains the same study with 20 result sets and 20 participants; the checklist introduces no revised protocol.

E4.justification: The BiDiFuse and part-consistency-loss ablations in Table 1 and Section 4.2 are identical. Appendix E retains the same architecture comparison and discussion of unsuccessful structural priors, and the qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed/run counts. New checklist item 7 acknowledges and explains this existing omission, but adds no uncertainty estimates or changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4 and the qualitative findings are retained. For example, SP4D's multi-view/multi-frame mIoU remains 0.68/0.70 in Table 1, and its rigging precision remains 72.7 in Table 4.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, fusion equation, contrastive objective, and harmonic skinning boundary-value formulation are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint RGB/kinematic-part generation, generalization, mesh lifting, and KinematicParts20K. The checklist's qualification about incomplete automatic rigging restates an existing boundary.

C2.justification: The new checklist explicitly attributes missing statistical evaluation to cost and limited study participation, and clarifies that no safeguard implementation or detailed description is provided. Existing mechanism explanations and camera/multi-object limitations in Appendix E are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page address and explicitly states in checklist item 5 that the authors cannot commit to releasing code. These clarify access information; implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and data-processing instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The research references, related-work discussion, novelty positioning, and Appendix E comparisons with prior approaches are unchanged. The added checklist contains policy links rather than new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a NeurIPS checklist between the references and supplement, updates the publication footer, and corrects SPD to SP4D in the Figure 1 caption. The existing scientific narrative and appendix prose are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives small rendering and label changes. Figure 4 is reduced slightly and the existing Figure 5 moves from page 9 to page 8, causing subsequent text to reflow. Tables and the scientific content of the figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The project-page pointer and explicit disclosures about code-release uncertainty and missing statistical evaluation modestly improve transparency over v1. These are limited documentation gains: the scientific evidence, reproducibility details, and statistical limitations remain unchanged.
